messages:
maria: heads-up — longctx stress runs show monotonic VRAM growth when paged KV + async-evict enabled on MI250X. repro gist coming.
jon: can you paste minimal repro and perf counters?
maria: repro steps:
```
./tests/longctx_paged_kv --model t5x --seq 32 --long-context 1000000 --async-evict=1 --kernel-policy=auto
```
also attaching allocator dump, but gist: free_pages drops slowly, rss_full increases steadily across runs.
jon: can you paste allocator counts (pte_allocated, pte_free, refs)?
maria: pt_alloc=128k, pt_free=2k, pte_refs_high=~320M ops; observed growth ~+0.5% VRAM per 1k steps.
sasha: did we roll the tiled-kernel fallback last friday? kernel-selection v2 went live then.
maria: yes — interestingly this only reproduces with kernel=v2 (tiled fallback enabled). kernel=v1 (legacy linear kernels) is stable.
oliver: eviction traces look like out-of-order completions — evict scheduled but pte refcount not decremented before remap. snippet: 
```
[evict] page=0x7f3a refs=1 -> evict scheduled
[remap] page=0x7f3a remap->owner=2 refs++ (still 1)
[evict-complete] page=0x7f3a free called but ref==1 -> leak
```
kevin: sounds like a serialization gap between kernel launch and completion callback on the tiled path. maybe the tiled kernel uses a different completion record / stream and we miss ordering.
maria: confirmed locally: adding an explicit stream-synchronize in eviction completion handler stops the growth (local hack), but that's a heavy perf hit.
jon: ok can we add a lightweight fence or enforce release semantics on the refcount updates? try switching `atomic_add_relaxed` -> `atomic_add_release` on remap path.
sasha: can you bisect kernel-selection? force tiled vs linear on H100 and MI250X and measure growth curves. we need cross-arch comparison.
maria: starting bisect on MI250X now, will run pair on H100 tomorrow and post numbers.
infra-bot: perf-job #3421 triggered: longctx-paged-kv/mi250x/bisect run started — https://ci.redwood/perf/3421
maria: quick TL;DR — leak only when (1) tiled kernel fallback is active and (2) async-evict enabled. hypothesis: tiled kernel uses different completion record path that can race with page-table refcount update during remap/evict.
oliver: should we revert kernel-selection v2 for MI family until we have a fix? or add guard to disable async-evict for tiled kernels only?
kevin: safer to guard async-evict when kernel==tiled; I'll open a small PR with a runtime guard + additional logging.
jon: I can run microbench comparing release vs relaxed atomic ordering tomorrow and share perf delta.
maria: thanks — attaching raw traces + small repro here: https://gist.github.com/xxxxx. posting updates as bisect runs. :eyes:
